scope: Independent verification of consequential investigator claims for the released plan; source IDs preserved as originally assigned, with S16 added as a separate pinned upstream cross-check.

sources.title: SQLite FTS5 official manual
sources.version_or_commit: Living official manual; no revision/commit exposed.
sources.locator: Sections 2, 4.3, 4.4, 6.7, 6.12–6.13; contentless-delete, external content, tokenizer, integrity-check, rebuild, secure-delete.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official manual at contentless-delete and external-content sections; reviewed tokenizer, integrity-check, rebuild and secure-delete passages.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: FTS5 availability is build-dependent. unicode61 is default; external-content sync remains application responsibility; integrity comparison for external content requires rank=1; REBUILD uses a content source and is unavailable for contentless tables. Contentless-delete is a distinct mode added at 3.43.0.
sources.applicability: Supports the draft's SQLite storage, tokenization, integrity and rebuild qualifications; actual packaged SQLite remains unknown.

sources.title: SQLite 3.43.0 release notes
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official release note and verified the contentless-delete item.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The mode is available from 3.43.0; earlier SQLite builds do not meet this feature floor.
sources.applicability: Supports the version gate; does not show the application's bundled version.

sources.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging
sources.version_or_commit: Living official manual; WAL support introduced in 3.7.0.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official WAL documentation at concurrency and checkpointing passages.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WAL allows readers and writers to overlap, but there is only one writer; long readers can delay checkpoint progress; WAL requires same-host shared-memory coordination.
sources.applicability: Supports measured, bounded rebuild/update concurrency; not a promise of zero save contention.

sources.title: SQLite compile-time options
sources.version_or_commit: Living official manual; app build unknown.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the compile-options page and verified the FTS5 amalgamation build flag.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: FTS5 is included when the option is defined for amalgamation builds; package availability cannot be inferred from SQLite API presence alone.
sources.applicability: Supports runtime/packaging gate in the draft.

sources.title: SQLite forum: Unicode61 Polish Ł/ł
sources.version_or_commit: Official SQLite forum, posts 2020-05-11 to 2021-02-23; reporter initially used SQLite 3.30.1.
sources.locator: Posts 1–5, especially maintainer Dan Kennedy at post 3.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the SQLite-hosted forum and read the reporter and maintainer explanation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The Unicode data entries for Ł/ł have no base-L decomposition; remove_diacritics does not make Ł equivalent to L in this case; maintainer suggests a custom tokenizer.
sources.applicability: Concrete counterexample only; supports explicit equivalence fixtures, not a generalized tokenizer defect.

sources.title: SQLite bug forum: nested AFTER UPDATE and external-content FTS5
sources.version_or_commit: Official SQLite bug-forum report opened 2026-08-04; reproduction reports SQLite 3.45.1, 3.45.3 and 3.53.2.
sources.locator: Corrected reproduction and maintainer explanation, posts 3–4.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the thread; read corrected reproduction, test condition and maintainer response.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Narrow interaction: a second AFTER UPDATE trigger issues a nested write to the same content table alongside FTS sync. The maintainer confirms trigger invocation can make the content table show newer values when sync logic reads it; trigger order/workaround is qualified.
sources.applicability: Supports the draft's bounded trigger caveat and need to test the actual trigger graph; does not support a claim that all external-content sync is unsafe.

sources.title: Tantivy 0.26.2 IndexWriter API
sources.version_or_commit: Crate 0.26.2; VCS identity as stated by the investigator source map: 72d1ef9a6468aa68bbc69dcc80cdf60aaf64364d.
sources.observed_operation: Opened version-pinned API at commit and delete methods.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Commit blocks and publishes pending documents; deletes affect prior commits and earlier operations in the same commit and appear after commit; add may block when the pipeline is full.
sources.applicability: Supports writer batching, publication watermark and asynchronous-worker design.

sources.title: Tantivy 0.26.2 IndexReader API
sources.version_or_commit: Crate 0.26.2; same pinned source identity as S08.
sources.observed_operation: Opened version-pinned reader API at reload and searcher methods.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Default commit reload is rapid but can take tens of milliseconds; one searcher should be used consistently for each query.

sources.title: Tantivy 0.26.2 tokenizer module
sources.version_or_commit: Crate 0.26.2; same pinned source identity as S08.
sources.locator: default and en_stem tokenizer sections; custom filters.
sources.observed_operation: Opened tokenizer documentation and reviewed defaults and analyzer composition.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Default splits punctuation/whitespace, lowercases and drops tokens longer than 40 characters; en_stem is English-specific and documented as slower; custom tokenizers are possible.
sources.applicability: Supports limits and need for per-script fixtures, not a claim of multilingual segmentation.

sources.title: Tantivy 0.26.2 delete/update package-source locator
sources.observed_operation: Attempted the carried docs.rs source URL; web returned an internal error. Cross-checked the same commit-pinned source file via S16; original URL and S11 identity are retained.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: No direct primary-ID enforcement; the example models update as delete plus reinsert and commits before reload.
sources.applicability: Evidence was independently checked at S16, not silently rebound to a different S11 URL.

sources.title: Tantivy 0.26.2 changelog
sources.locator: Tantivy 0.24 compatibility statement; historical 0.13 and 0.11 reindex notes.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the pinned changelog and searched/read release compatibility and reindex entries.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The changelog names specific compatibility pairs and historical releases requiring reindex; those do not establish universal compatibility.
sources.applicability: Supports versioned format/rebuild fallback without a universal upgrade claim.

sources.title: Tantivy 0.26.2 upstream delete/update example at pinned commit
sources.version_or_commit: Exact commit 72d1ef9a6468aa68bbc69dcc80cdf60aaf64364d, corresponding to Tantivy crate 0.26.2 per investigator S14.
sources.locator: Comments and code around lines 559–675 and 683–706.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the exact commit-pinned upstream source file and read ID uniqueness, delete+add, commit and reader reload passages.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Example explicitly says there is no primary-ID enforcement and demonstrates an indexed ID field, delete then reinsert, commit, reload, and assertions. It is a source example, not a notebook benchmark.
